item.title: Age of AI news and its influence: Where do we go from here? | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: A recent study by communications psychologists at University College London found that participants who watched deepfake videos were still influenced by the content even after being told the videos were fabricated. Did you catch that?

item.title: Senate approves revised bill focused on penalties for school threats | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: Alabama senators approved last week a bill that would strengthen criminal penalties for school threats and require students charged with making them to be removed from the regular classroom until a hearing is held.

item.description: Members of Alabama’s Student Retention Council recently told state lawmakers they are working to raise awareness of career opportunities and quality-of-life advantages in hopes of persuading more graduates to stay in Alabama.

item.title: Birmingham-area churches host city's first Serve Tour, see big impact | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: During Birmingham Serve Tour, more than 1,400 volunteers from 15 states partnered with churches in the Birmingham metro area to work on more than 50 projects ranging from giving haircuts at shelters to building bed kits.

item.title: Nearing final passage on title fraud prevention bill | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: The Alabama Legislature is close to final passage on bills supporters hope will protect property owners by making it harder for fraudsters to sell real estate they don’t own.

item.title: Alabama CHOOSE Act applications exceed 37,000; March 31 deadline approaching | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: Alabama’s school voucher program has drawn more than 37,000 applications for the 2026-27 school year, outpacing last year’s mid-March total even as the number of first-time applicants trails last year’s pace.

item.title: Central Alabama Water to stop adding fluoride to drinking water | The Alabama Baptist
item.description: Birmingham-area water filtration company Central Alabama Water will stop adding fluoride to its drinking water, it announced recently.
